messages:
maria_support: FYI tenant `brightloop` reporting sustained p95 token latency + 429s starting ~2024-11-08T09:12Z on `eu1-dedicated-pool-7`. Dashboard shows queue depth rising and autoscale not triggering fast enough.
sam_sre: Can you paste the short metric snippet and any request ids? :eyes:
maria_support: metrics: p95 token latency 1.2s -> 4.6s, 429 rate from 0% -> 6% over 20m, inflight queue 2 -> 45, worker_retries spike. Sample req id: req_0a1f2b3c. Node assigned: node-eu1-gpu-17 (MIG config: 1g.10gb + 3g.6gb slices). Attaching nvml sample:
```
Time  GPU  SM%  MEM%  ENC%  DEC%  FB_MiB  BW_GB/s
09:18  0    98    89    0     0    9478    38.4
09:19  0    99    91    0     0    9531    39.0
```
maria_support: Also see occasional `429` entries in api-proxy logs: `rate limit exceeded` but tenant is on Dedicated. Suspect internal backpressure from runtime queuing.
josh_mlinfra: Could be MIG cross-talk on memory BW or PCIe saturation. The 1g+3g mixed slices on same physical GPU sometimes causes uneven BW arbitration. Did we see NVLink or GPU fabric errors?
maria_support: No GPU ECC or fatal errs. PCIe util occasionally high. dmesg shows some warnings: `mmc: pcie err - link retrain` (small). No evictions reported from k8s.
olivia_eng: Two quick asks: (1) can we repro with a constrained synthetic load to confirm bandwidth sensitivity? (2) can we temporarily move brightloop to an isolated host? Sam, do we have spare capacity?
sam_sre: We have one spare node in eu1-dedicated-pool-9. I can move them if they approve. For repro: run 200 concurrent small requests (seq length ~128) and measure p95. Use the load tool below.
tenant_ops: We'll give approval for a short maintenance migration. Our SLOs are degraded.
josh_mlinfra: Repro steps (quick):
```
# ramp to 200 concurrency
hey -n 20000 -c 200 -H "Authorization: Bearer <tenant-key>" https://api.eu1.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# check GPU perf
ssh node-eu1-gpu-17 'nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 1 -c 10'
```
Look for sustained FB bandwidth near card max and SM util at 95% while latency climbs.
sam_sre: Mitigation options:
- migrate tenant to pool-9 host (manual drain)
- temporarily bump `autoscale.min_replicas` +1 for their route
- pin to a larger MIG slice if available (1g -> 2g) while we investigate
olivia_eng: If we migrate, also rotate the tenant's node binding so scheduler doesn't binpack back. Use `rictl transfer-tenant --tenant brightloop --to-pool eu1-dedicated-pool-9` (dry-run first).
maria_support: Running dry-run now... returns: `ok -> target node candidate node-eu1-gpu-23`.
deploy-bot: Notice: rolling transfer job queued (job id jt_20241108_09_45).
sam_sre: I just started a manual autoscale bump for brightloop route (min_replicas +1) — should pop in ~30s. Watch dashboards.
maria_support: Autoscale bump applied. p95 dropped from 4.6s -> 2.1s in 90s, 429s fell to 1.2%.
tenant_ops: Good improvement. We'll accept short migration if it stabilizes to baseline.
josh_mlinfra: Longer-term: ops to consider strict MIG slicing strategy per tenant (homogeneous slices on host), and adding BW isolation flags at runtime. Filing a follow-up infra task.
olivia_eng: FYI also saw a couple of 401s in the tenant logs earlier — likely a transient token refresh race during retries. Nothing linked to the GPU noise but call it out to tenant.
sam_sre: Next steps: (1) finish migration, (2) capture full `nvidia-smi dmon` trace for 15m, (3) open infra ticket INFRA-3061 to evaluate MIG placement policy and autoscale reaction tuning.
maria_support: I'll attach logs and the dmon trace to INFRA-3061 and ping tenant about planned migration window.
tenant_ops: Thanks team, keep us posted. :thumbsup:
olivia_eng: Great triage. Adding `:eyes:` to follow-up ticket. If this recurs after migration we'll schedule a deeper kernel/firmware check.
sam_sre: Marking thread resolved for now — reopen if p95 climbs back after migration.
file_notes: Slack thread about noisy neighbor causing p95 spikes and 429s in a dedicated pool; includes repro steps, nvml snippet, short-term mitigation and follow-ups
